title: S02 CAPTURE lane: the opening, photographed
_comment: CAPTURE lane for S02. There is nothing to seed it with: §B gives S01 the entry save 'none (fresh)' and S02 the handoff 'in-memory', so the chapter's first slot file does not exist until this segment's own play makes it. The front door IS the only production path to every state here, which is why this lane is a replay of the opening rather than a load and a walk.
_comment_generated: GENERATED by tools/gate_f/derive_capture_lane.py from S02.json. Do not hand-edit: change the source segment or the authored notes in the generator and regenerate, or the capture lane stops being the journey's own path and §H.1's provenance claim stops being true. `--check` fails CI-style if the two have drifted.
_comment_derivation: Kept: every step of S02 up to and including its last capture (index 59 of 74), minus note/defect/probe_cell/save_out and the four pacing asserts. 53 of 75 steps survive. Step ids carry their origin in `_derived_from`.
_comment_seeding: Run this into the SAME run directory as the logic lanes. Its `seed_save` steps resolve `run://` against that directory's saves, so a capture lane run anywhere else has no chapter to load and will stop at its first seed.
_comment_cost: The most expensive kind of capture lane in the run and the one the split cannot help: eight frames, seven of them behind the wake beat, the Grandpa conversation, the starter choice, a named creature, a first ambush and a first catch. Sixty of S02's seventy-five steps are kept. On a GPU host that is a few minutes of play; on this container it is the ~8,283-hour envelope and must not be attempted.

GF-02-START-01.why: the wake beat is what Start New Game lands on. No save precedes it because none can. Cost is a boot plus the ~90 s cold Meadows stand-up, not a boot.

GF-21-WEATHER-01.why: 'each weather preset first naturally encountered'. Which preset is up at the wake beat is the world clock's business, and §0.6 bars pin_clock outside a DIAG segment, so this lane photographs whatever weather the restaged opening produced -- not necessarily the one the journey saw.

GF-02-START-02.why: mid-dialogue with Grandpa. A narrative modal is not a saveable state; the conversation is restaged by walking into it exactly as the journey did.

GF-02-START-03.why: the starter picker open with an orb focused. Same class as the dialogue, and the focused index is a live UI state no slot file carries.

GF-14-COMBAT-01.why: CB-01, the first ambush. A fight in progress; the lane re-fights it.

GF-15-CATCH-01.why: the aim reticle up mid-throw. The most transient state in the protocol.

GF-15-CATCH-02.why: the catch resolving. Same throw, six seconds later; a restage that fails to catch produces a frame of a different outcome, and that has to be read off the frame rather than assumed.

GF-03-VILLAGE-01.why: first arrival at the village centre (10,-10) is a PLACE, and would be a cheap class B from any save -- but no save exists this early in the chapter, so reaching it costs the whole opening. A place frame priced like an event frame, purely because of where the save chain starts.

steps.title: open with the charged attack, at full health
steps.expected: Section E.1 CB-01 records duration, attacks/damage exchanges, camera corrections, target_on_screen dropouts and the difficulty read. Combat is real-time and directly piloted (D07)
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 MEASURED, twice, superseding this step's stale note (~5.8 dmg/hit -- damage was rebalanced since it was written). Quick attacks land ~12-13.4; the charged lands ~56; the practice bramblebun rolls 104-124 HP depending on the boot. RUN6 attempt 1 ran 6 quick then the charged: 104.3 -> 91.3 -> 78.0 -> 63.8 -> 49.4 -> 0.0, the charged FAINTED it and the catch had nothing to throw at. Attempt 2 ran 1 quick then the charged, the charged missed (cone 75 deg, range 3.0, the target had moved), the throw went at 90% HP where `catching.json`'s hp_factor is 0.10, and it failed. So the charged is now taken FIRST, at full health where it cannot faint anything, and the quick attacks trim afterwards: charged ~56 then 2 quick ~25 leaves 23-43 HP (23-35%) on either roll -- alive on both, and well up the hp_factor curve.

steps.title: trim with quick attacks
steps.expected: Section E.4: `combat_charged` is a hold-to-charge verb; the long hold is what distinguishes it from the quick attack
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6, fourth measurement. The retry blocks below re-enter `combat_aim` (the telemetry shows ctx=combat_aim on each retry press) but NO second `catch_throw` is ever emitted -- three retries, three re-aims, zero throws, across two runs. Recorded as an open defect (GAME-11/RIG-26); it means the `max_catch_failures: 1` guarantee, which only bites on the SECOND landed throw, is currently unreachable. Until that is root-caused the segment cannot rely on the pity bound, so the FIRST throw has to carry the catch: the charged attack plus three quick attacks lands ~95 damage on a creature that rolls 104-124 HP, leaving 9-29 HP (9-23%), which is high up `catching.json`'s hp_factor curve without fainting either roll.

steps.title: begin the aim
steps.expected: docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md beat 8: 'The catch is a physical act you aim'. CONTROLLER-MAP put the orb on the hotbar and throws it with interact, so X reaches `_try_throw` through `interact`
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6, third measurement: `combat_manager.gd:1273` applies `catch_math.apply_failure_bound()` once `_tutorial_catch_failure_bound >= 0`, so with `max_catch_failures: 1` the SECOND LANDED throw is forced to succeed. The binding constraint is therefore not catch odds -- it is keeping the fight alive long enough for two throws to land. A lvl-3 starter (117 HP) against a practice bramblebun that rolls lvl 5 / 124 HP loses a long exchange: one RUN6 run ended with Moss at 0.0 HP and the fight over before the retries could throw. So the pre-catch damage is cut to the charged attack plus a single quick (both verbs still exercised for section E.4, ~69 dmg, leaving 34-44% HP on either roll), and the throw sequence is entered sooner and retried three times.

With `max_catch_failures: 1` the game's promise is kept on the second landed throw, so asserting after throw 1 reads a legitimate first failure as a defect -- which is exactly how this segment reported 'party size 1 (wanted 2)' in a run whose own exit save carried a party of 2. steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit. A walk that begins while a narrative modal still owns input does not fail as 'a modal is open' -- it fails as 'did not reach', many steps and sometimes many minutes later, which is how X04 lost its whole combat block to 3601 held frames. This assert is diagnostic and changes no behaviour: it turns that silent cascade into one named cause at the point of origin. RIG-25's rule, applied to narrative modals rather than to shop panels.

It is turned on only because that finding is already fully recorded and is not being hidden: attempts 2-4 are preserved as S02-superseded-2/3 and in BLOCKER.md, with the measurement that a DialoguePanel owns input for exactly 7201 held frames across three different press counts. A developer probe (tools/opening_fix/probe_named_hold.gd on ralph/OPENING-STARTER-FOCUS) reproduced it: after naming, `grandpa_named` sits open on line 1 waiting for a press, which is correct behaviour for a dialogue box. What answers it here is the same interact tap a player makes. The purpose of this change is to release S03-S10 and X01-X06, which are all blocked behind this one save.
